Dave Baulch, again selected to run up Dale Hill, joined in the spirit of the chase and soon moved up to third place and was gaining fast on Woodford, who had by this time run all their best men and were beginning to flag badly.

This year we have missed the assistance of Chas. Walker, Dave Baulch, Brian Hallowell and others. We must thank our second claim member, Len Orton, for his support at our fixtures.

No sooner had the second lap commenced than Pat decided to increase the tempo, only Dave Baulch attempting to go with him. However,on leaving the Common for Copse Hill Pat was way ahead and increasing his lead with every stride; the role of pack leader being taken over by Eric Gebbett.
On the first leg Dave Baulch ran 13.42 to set up a new Club best, only to be 250 yds. behind the leader, Roath(Walton), who sliced 16s. off the course record with a magnificent 13.01.
Dave Baulch, usually on a later stage, was having a change of scenery this year but as he was surrounded by Internationals he not surprisingly had to relinquish two vital places.
Our six were Bob Glover, Malcolm Robinson, Alan Black, Eric Gebbett, Charlie Walker and Dave Baulch; three relative newcomers to road relay racing and three "veterans".
A notable non-starter was Dave Baulch, suffering from a heavy cold, who, despite the assertions of the old-timers that a race would do him good, wisely refrained from competing.

Dave Baulch and Chas. Walker were well to the fore early on, and with Colin Collis, Archie Bedford, Len Bishop and Bob Plummer quite well placed, it seemed as if we might gain a team place in this well contested race.

Dave Baulch took the first stage and brought us in a creditable fourth in 18m.3s., twenty-three seconds behind the leaders, Thames Valley. Eric Gebbett ran the second stage in 18.45 and took us up to third with T.V.H. still in first place, forty-three seconds ahead.

Next came Dave Baulch, making his last appearance for Belgrave (so he says), and he set off as though he really meant Belgrave to reach Brighton first.

Dave Baulch took second place and Malcolm Robinson was third. We visited Cranford for the T.V.H. road relay on Easter Saturday and started four teams but were without a number of our best performers, and in consequence were not in the running for leading honours.
With the return of George Flannagan to active training, the hope of a 'come-back' by Dave Baulch and the prospect of an active season from Ron Linstead our potential is indeed great.

En Route, Tom Carter's 10 mile Club Record of 20 odd years standing went by the board, with 52.06,and 11½ miles were covered in the hour; bettering Dave Baulch's hour record by no less than 450 yards!

Tony Fairclough had different ideas on the subject and caring little for the reputation of Frank Salvat,produced the best ever run by a Belgrave Harrier on this leg;and in knocking four seconds from Dave Baulch's club record became the first Belgravian to beat twenty minutes.
Names to disappear are:- Dave Baulch, Charlie Smart, Barry Sawyer, John Dear, Mal Robinson, Pete Bagnall, John Bromley, Ray Tooby, Archie Bedford and Kelly Diprose.
